name: Tenmonkan
tagline: The covered arcades and the shochu bars
description: The commercial and entertainment heart of the city, a grid of covered shopping arcades with the izakaya, shochu specialists and restaurants that make Kagoshima's evenings. The tram runs through it and the ferry to Sakurajima is a short walk east.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the food and drink on the doorstep
pros: The city's best eating and drinking
Covered arcades, useful in rain and heat
Tram and Sakurajima ferry both close
cons: The busiest and noisiest part of the city
Volcanic ash collects in the streets

name: Kagoshima-Chuo Station
tagline: The Shinkansen terminus and the newer development
description: The area around the main station, terminus of the Kyushu Shinkansen, with the Amu Plaza complex and its ferris wheel, hotels and a growing cluster of restaurants. It is the most practical base for anyone moving around Kyushu.
bestFor: Short stays and anyone travelling by Shinkansen
pros: Hotels and shopping in one complex
cons: Ten minutes from the main nightlife
Busy and impersonal around the station

name: Shiroyama and Terukuni
tagline: The hill above the city and the Saigo sites
description: The wooded hill immediately behind the centre, with the observation point that looks straight across at Sakurajima, the cave where Saigo Takamori made his last stand, and the Terukuni shrine at its foot. Residential streets sit on the slopes below.
bestFor: Anyone wanting the volcano view and quiet close to the centre
pros: The best view of Sakurajima in the city
Wooded hill walks minutes from the centre
Saigo Takamori sites and the shrine

name: Iso and Sengan-en
tagline: The Shimadzu garden on the coast north of town
description: The coastal strip north of the centre around Sengan-en, the Shimadzu clan's garden laid out in 1658 with Sakurajima borrowed as its backdrop, and the Shoko Shuseikan industrial museum beside it, both UNESCO listed. Residential streets run behind them.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting the coast and the garden nearby
pros: Sengan-en and the UNESCO industrial sites
cons: Ash fall is heavier on this side

name: Sakurajima
description: The peninsula across the bay, fifteen minutes by ferry, where a few thousand people live on the slopes of an active volcano among lava fields, hot springs and the famous giant radishes. The ferry runs around the clock, which makes it genuinely commutable.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to say they lived on an active volcano
pros: Ferry to the city runs twenty-four hours
Hot springs, lava fields and observatories
Far cheaper than the city side
cons: Heaviest ash fall anywhere in the area
Evacuation planning is a real part of life
